decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Manual bookmark creation.” Round 1 client: “saving links … That's the heart of what I want.”
decisions.note: The specification includes URL-based bookmark creation, consistent with the reference at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Tags.” Round 1 client: “tagging them.”
decisions.note: Tag assignment is included at the specification gate; no conflicting behavior is presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “search.” Round 1 client: “searching.”
decisions.note: General bookmark search is included at the specification gate. The presentation does not make a contrary decision about searchable fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “filtering.” Round 1 client: “filtering.”
decisions.note: Filtering is included alongside tags at the specification gate, with no presented contradiction.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “sorting.” Round 1 client: “sorting.”
decisions.note: List sorting is included at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “archiving.” Round 1 client: “archiving.”
decisions.note: Archiving is included at the specification gate; no contradictory archive behavior is stated.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Editing.” Round 1 client: “editing.”
decisions.note: Bookmark editing is included at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “confirmed deletion.” Round 1 client: “deleting with a confirmation step.”
decisions.note: Permanent deletion is included; requiring confirmation is an orthogonal safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Duplicate URL detection.” Round 1 client approves “catching duplicate links.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, detection is stated but the presentation does not establish whether duplicate saving guides the user to edit the existing bookmark. Approval does not resolve that uncertainty.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “browser import/export … currently out of scope.” Round 1 client approves without mentioning import.
decisions.note: Excluding browser-bookmark import departs from the required Netscape HTML import feature at the specification gate; the client does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “browser import/export … currently out of scope.” Round 1 client approves without mentioning export.
decisions.note: Excluding browser-bookmark export departs from the required Netscape HTML export feature at the specification gate; the client does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “automatic page metadata [is] currently out of scope.” Round 1 client: “I'd assumed that when I paste in a link, the app would fill in the title … I can live with that for a first version, so no need to change it.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly identifies the expected automatic-title behavior and accepts its deferral at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker excludes “automatic page metadata.” Round 1 client discusses only automatic title fill-in and says nothing about description, favicon, or preview-image collection.
decisions.note: Automatic description, favicon, and preview-image collection are separable parts of the excluded metadata decision. The client explicitly accepts only the title departure, leaving these differences unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Automatic title retrieval remains deferred for a later feature.” Round 2 client: “automatic title fill-in is being left for later, which is fine by me.”
decisions.note: At the implementation-plan gate, the client again explicitly acknowledges and accepts the automatic-title departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “11 tasks for saving and revisiting bookmarks” and MVP includes “persistent bookmark saving.” Round 3 client: “saving and reopening links.”
decisions.note: The task plan includes bookmark saving, conforming at the task-planning stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: tasks for “revisiting bookmarks” and MVP includes “reopening links.” Round 3 client: “saving and reopening links.”
decisions.note: The task plan includes reopening original links, consistent with navigation to the bookmarked URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “8 tasks for tags, search, filters, and sorting.” Round 3 client: “tags with search, filters and sorting.”
decisions.note: Tag functionality remains included at the task-planning stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “8 tasks for tags, search, filters, and sorting.” Round 3 client approves the search work.
decisions.note: Search remains included at the task-planning stage, with no presented conflicting behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “8 tasks for tags, search, filters, and sorting.” Round 3 client approves “filters.”
decisions.note: Filtering remains included alongside tags at the task-planning stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “8 tasks for tags, search, filters, and sorting.” Round 3 client approves “sorting.”
decisions.note: Sorting remains included at the task-planning stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “10 tasks for editing ….” Round 3 client approves “the editing … work.”
decisions.note: Bookmark editing remains included at the task-planning stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “10 tasks for … archiving.” Round 3 client approves “archiving.”
decisions.note: Archiving remains included at the task-planning stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “10 tasks for … confirmed deletion.” Round 3 client approves “confirmed deletion work.”
decisions.note: Deletion remains included at the task-planning stage; confirmation is an additional safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: MVP includes “duplicate detection.” Round 3 client says the breakdown aligns and approves implementation.
decisions.note: The task presentation does not independently establish whether detection includes guidance to edit the existing bookmark. The approval does not clarify that pending behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “Persistent bookmark saving.” Round 4 client: “I saved a link … and it showed up in my collection.”
decisions.note: Bookmark saving is presented as delivered and is consistent with the reference at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “saving and reopening.” Round 4 client says the application does what was needed.
decisions.note: Reopening saved links is presented as delivered, consistent with navigating to the original URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “Tags.” Round 4 client: “I saved a link with … tags.”
decisions.note: Tag assignment is presented as delivered at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “search.” Round 4 client: “Searching found it.”
decisions.note: Bookmark search is presented as delivered, with no stated conflicting search behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “filters.” Round 4 client accepts the completed application.
decisions.note: Filtering is presented as delivered alongside tags at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “four sorting modes.” Round 4 client accepts the completed application.
decisions.note: Multiple list-sorting modes conform to the sorting requirement at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “archive/restore” and separately “confirmed deletion.” Round 4 client: “archiving … worked, deleting removed it.”
decisions.note: The delivered presentation distinguishes reversible archive/restore from deletion, conforming to the archive and archive-versus-delete decisions.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “Editing.” Round 4 client accepts the application as the desired first version.
decisions.note: Bookmark editing is presented as delivered at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “confirmed deletion.” Round 4 client: “deleting removed it.”
decisions.note: Deletion is presented as delivered; confirmation is an orthogonal safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “Normalized duplicate-link detection.” Round 4 client: “it stopped me and pointed me at the one I already had.”
decisions.note: The maker's implementation presentation independently establishes detection but does not specify whether the pointer guides the user into editing the existing bookmark. The client describes the observed result approvingly but does not state the reference expectation or a corrective/accepting disposition about edit guidance, so divergence remains indeterminate.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “Automatic title retrieval remains intentionally deferred.” Round 4 client: “the automatic title fill-in we agreed to leave for later is the only thing I'd still like down the road.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, the client explicitly identifies the missing automatic-title behavior and accepts the departure for this first version.
